source_text: Κἀγὼ εἶπον· Ὡς ὑμῖν φίλον, πράξω. Ἀπὸ μὲν οὖν τῶν ἐξηγήσεων, ὧν ἐξηγήσατο Ἔσδρας εἰς τὸν νόμον τὸν περὶ τοῦ πάσχα, τὴν ἐξήγησιν ταύτην ἀφείλοντο· Καὶ εἶπεν Ἔσδρας τῷ λαῷ· Τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ καταφυγὴ ἡμῶν. Καὶ ἐὰν διανοηθῆτε καὶ ἀναβῇ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν, ὅτι μέλλομεν αὐτὸν ταπεινοῦν ἐν σημείῳ, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐλπίσωμεν ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, οὐ μὴ ἐρημωθῇ ὁ τόπος οὗτος εἰς τὸν ἅπαντα χρόνον, λέγει ὁ θεὸς τῶν δυνάμεων· ἂν δὲ μὴ πιστεύσητε αὐτῷ μηδὲ εἰσακούσητε τοῦ κηρύγματος αὐτοῦ. ἔσεσθε ἐπίχαρμα τοῖς ἔθνεσι [Esdr. ?]. Καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν διὰ Ἱερεμίου λεχθέντων ταῦτα περιέκοψαν· Ἐγὼ ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον. φερόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι. Ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ ἐλογίζοντο λογισμόν, λέγοντες· Δεῦτε, ἐμβάλωμεν ξύλον εἰς τὸν ἄρτον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκτρίψωμεν αὐτὸν ἐκ γῆς ζώντων, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ μνησθῇ οὐκέτι [JÉR., XI, 19]. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ αὕτη ή περικοπή, ἡ ἐκ τῶν λόγων τοῦ Ἱερεμίου, ἔτι ἐστὶν ἐγγεγραμμένη ἔν τισιν ἀντιγράφοις τῶν ἐν συναγωγαῖς Ἰουδαίων (πρὸ γὰρ ὀλίγου χρόνου ταῦτα ἐξέκοψαν), ἐπειδὰν καὶ ἐκ τούτων τῶν λόγων ἀποδεικνύηται ὅτι ἐβουλεύσαντο Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀναιρεῖν αὐτὸν σταυρώσαντες βουλευσάμενοι, καὶ αὐτὸς μηνύεται, ὡς καὶ διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου προεφητεύθη, ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἀγόμενος , καὶ ἐνθάδε ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον δηλοῦται· ὥστ᾿ ἀπορούμενοι ἐπὶ τὸ βλασφημεῖν χωροῦσι. Καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἱερεμίου ὁμοίως ταῦτα περιέκοψαν· Ἐμνήσθη δὲ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἅγιος Ἰσραὴλ τῶν νεκρῶν αὐτοῦ, τῶν κεκοιμημένων εἰς γῆν χώματος, καὶ κατέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτοῖς τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ [JÉR. ? cf. I Pierre, III, 19, et IV. 6].
pass_a_gloss: And I said, As is dear to you, I will do. From the explanations, which Ezra explained concerning the law of the passover, they removed this explanation: And Ezra said to the people, This passover is our Savior and our refuge. And if you think and it comes up into your heart, that we are going to humble him in a sign, and after these things we hope in him, this place will not be deserted for all time, says the God of the powers; but if you do not believe in him nor listen to his proclamation, you will be a laughingstock to the nations. And from the things spoken through Jeremiah these things were cut out: I am like an innocent lamb being led to be sacrificed. They devised a plan against me, saying, Come, let us put wood into his bread and let us trip him up from the land of the living, and his name will not be remembered anymore. And since this pericope, which is from the words of Jeremiah, is still written in some copies of the synagogue of the Jews (for they cut these things out a little while ago), when even from these words it is demonstrated that the Jews planned to kill Christ, having crucified him with a plan, and he himself is indicated, as also was prophesied through Isaiah, as a sheep being led to slaughter, and here as an innocent lamb he is revealed; thus being at a loss they proceed to blaspheme. And from the words of the same Jeremiah these things were similarly cut out: And the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, remembered his dead, who had fallen asleep in the earth of dust, and he went down to them to evangelize them his salvation.

pass_b_english: I said, "I will do as you wish." They removed this explanation from the commentaries in which Ezra interpreted the law concerning the Passover: Ezra told the people, "This Passover is our Savior and our refuge. If you reflect and it enters your heart that we are going to humble him by a sign, and after these things we hope in him, this place will not be deserted for all time, says the God of hosts. But if you do not believe in him nor listen to his proclamation, you will be a laughingstock to the nations." They also cut out these words spoken through Jeremiah: "I was like an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed. They devised a plot against me, saying, 'Come, let us put wood into his bread and let us eradicate him from the land of the living, and his name will not be remembered anymore'" (Jer. 11:19). Since this pericope from the words of Jeremiah is still written in some copies of the Jewish synagogues (for they cut these things out a short time ago), it is demonstrated even from these words that the Jews plotted to kill Christ by crucifying him after planning it, and he himself is indicated as the one who was prophesied through Isaiah to be led like a sheep to slaughter, and here he is revealed as an innocent lamb; thus, being at a loss, they proceed to blaspheme. Similarly, they cut out these words from the same Jeremiah: "And the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, remembered his dead who had fallen asleep in the earth of dust, and he went down to them to proclaim the good news of his salvation to them" (cf. 1 Pet. 3:19; 4:6).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the nuances of the Jeremiah and Ezra passages. Pass B correctly identifies and expands the scripture citations (Jer. 11:19 and 1 Pet. 3:19; 4:6) as required by the instructions for added identifications. The distinction between 'trip him up' (Pass A) and 'eradicate him' (Pass B) for ἐκτρίψωμεν is a stylistic choice that does not violate the sense of the Greek in context.
